extensions.link.field: Web Store page, extension id, or a .crx / .zip link
extensions.link.help: A Web Store page is not the file itself, so the id is taken out of the address and the extension fetched by it. Pasting just the id works too.

fingerprints.intro: These FingerprintConfig snapshots populate the *GPU* select in the profile editor. Import your own from any working ShardX profile JSON to expand the list.
fingerprints.title: Fingerprint Library
incompatibleNotice.advice: Pick a fingerprint whose GPU family matches this machine, or run this one on a host that has the hardware.
incompatibleNotice.badgeModalTitle: This fingerprint does not fit this machine
incompatibleNotice.badgeTitle: This fingerprint does not fit this machine's GPU — click for why
incompatibleNotice.claimsIntro: This fingerprint claims a GPU your machine does not have, and asks for
incompatibleNotice.contradictionNote: The list says the extension is there and the object says it is not. That is not a weaker disguise — it is a self-contradiction, and it costs a detector two calls with no permission, no timing and no reference device. Anti-fraud systems check exactly this pair, because it is the cheapest way to catch a rewritten extension list.
incompatibleNotice.reportsListNote: The browser reports the profile's extension list, but it cannot make an extension work. So a page reads this:
incompatibleNotice.warningModalTitle: This fingerprint does not fit this machine
incompatibleNotice.webgpuNote: These behave differently from the extensions above: the browser does not claim them. It reports the profile's list narrowed to what this machine really has, so nothing contradicts itself — the adapter just reports a shorter list than the device the profile names would.
incompatibleNotice.webgpuUnbackedMany: {n} WebGPU features this machine cannot back:
incompatibleNotice.webgpuUnbackedOne: {n} WebGPU feature this machine cannot back:
patchlog.intro: What changed, and why. *Browser* entries live in the patched core itself — a page cannot tell them from what a stock Chromium does. *Launcher* entries are this app: what a profile is made of, and what it starts with.
patchlog.lock.body: The code is in the tree behind a build flag. Released binaries are built with it off, and the vocabulary is not compiled in either — a command name left in a shipped binary is exactly the kind of string that gets found and matched against a product.
patchlog.lock.ships: Ships at {n} stars on the repository
patchlog.title: Patch log
proxies.title: Proxies
settings.api.help: Local HTTP API (axum) for scripting — create/launch/close profiles and get a CDP WebSocket URL. Binds *127.0.0.1* only, JWT Bearer auth. Changes to enable/port apply after restarting the app.
settings.api.title: Automation API
settings.args.help:
Appended to every profile launch, one per line or space-separated. They go on *last*, so a switch repeated here is the one the engine sees — which is also how you get to undo one of the launcher's own. Quote a value with spaces.
Anything that changes what a page can measure belongs in the profile, not here: a switch applied to every profile at once makes them all alike, which is the opposite of what a profile is for.
settings.args.title: Extra launch arguments
settings.camera.help: The profile gets ShardX's camera instead of the machine's, and shows the picture or clip you pick from the control left of the browser's app menu. *Leave this on.* The profile's fingerprint already names a particular camera, so handing a page the host's real one contradicts the profile and identifies the machine behind every profile on it.
settings.camera.title: Profile camera
settings.dataRoot.title: Profile data location
settings.geo.help: Which free public IP-geo service to hit when you press the proxy *Test* button. All three are no-key, rate-limited.
settings.geo.label: Provider
settings.geo.title: Proxy geo checker
settings.helper.help:
Watches each page for fields a generated identity fits — names, email, phone, date of birth — and offers to fill them. It only ever *offers*: nothing is typed until you press the button on the panel that appears. Values come from the profile's own language, and go in through the same human typing the rest of the browser uses.
*Never runs on a synchronised launch.* In a group whatever you type in one window is mirrored into the others already, so a helper per window would find the same form ten times and offer ten prompts for one page.
settings.helper.title: Shard Helper
settings.helper.triggersHelp: Nothing selected means every kind. Narrow it if the panel appears on forms you do not care about — a login page with an email field is still a form.
settings.language.help: Which language the interface is written in. Screens not yet translated stay in English rather than showing their key names.
settings.language.label: Language
settings.language.title: Language
settings.mcp.help: Download the *MCP* server source (lets an AI client drive profiles and a CDP browser) into a folder you choose. The app does not run it — install its deps and register it with your MCP client per the included README. Requires Node.js.
settings.mcp.pickDownloadDir: Where to download the MCP server
settings.mcp.pickExistingDir: Select an existing ShardX MCP folder
settings.mcp.title: MCP server
settings.save.restartRequired: Restart required for Automation API changes
settings.screen.help: *From fingerprint* reports the screen carried in the bound profile (recommended for anti-detect coherence). *Real* lets ShardX expose the host monitor's actual size.

settings.whatsNew.help: After an update the launcher opens the patch log once, so the changes get seen before they surprise anyone. This reopens it on demand — useful when that first run went by in a hurry, or when someone else installed the update on this machine.
settings.whatsNew.title: What's new

trash.intro: A deleted profile waits here for seven days. What is kept is the account — cookies, logins, site storage, preferences — not the caches, so a profile that took a gigabyte comes back as a few megabytes.
trash.none.body: Deleted profiles land here and stay restorable for seven days.
trash.none.title: The trash is empty
trash.title: Trash
